weaknesses_found: The 'cold-start checkout' is not an independent clone: /Users/lge/Desktop/topic/leo-coldstart/.git is a file pointing at /Users/lge/Desktop/topic/leo-experiment-platform/.git/worktrees/leo-coldstart. It therefore shares the development repository's object store, refs and worktree admin files. Tests do not read any dev-worktree file (audit-hook run) and git status is empty, so no untracked-file dependency exists, but the checkout's very metadata depends on the dev repo: deleting/pruning the dev .git would break or corrupt it, and its 'cleanliness' is a property of a shared index. A true cold start should be a standalone clone or an archive of the commit.

SOURCE-COMMIT.txt inside the frozen checkout names 241627856886934cbbf2a0820982bef2018e6249, which does not exist in the object database (git cat-file: could not get object info). A cold-start reader following that file is pointed at a non-existent commit; the real identity is only in HEAD.

Residual silent-drop hole of the same family the fix closed: demand.burst_multiplier set under a mode that never applies the burst (verified with mode=uniform, multiplier 5.0, no window) resolves happily, keeps the value in the resolved config, and is silently ignored - no ConfigError and no diagnostic. burst_multiplier is likewise inert for diurnal/csv/population_gravity. The config gate covers burst_start_s/burst_duration_s but not the multiplier.

verify_burst_transform() is a 3-longitude x 6-time spot check: I replaced _rate_multiplier with a function that leaks the burst at every longitude except {0, 90, -180} and the trace compiled successfully, i.e. a transform that is wrong for most of the source population passes the 'deterministic correctness check'. It is a spot check, not the correctness proof the code comment claims ('the deterministic check above is what speaks to correctness').

The frozen TREE contains a superseded authorization: CODE/work/WP-LEO-V2-GLOBAL-PRESSURE-BRACKET/R01/authorization.json (tracked, pre-existing, not added by 324c8ee8). It binds code_sha256 daf695aff5ab443002e8969a89b6ca6948d343ed5fde1be790f247e7e65849ff (frozen value: 693796433f...) and v2_analysis.py 7b5e8418fc699aff10357e4c496696083840cb5503a346e2b6ed580fed7e6a18 (frozen: 9a74bb00ca...), authorises 2 runs, and its config_path does not exist in the tree. F9 is PASS on the commit's file list, but 'no old authorization is included' is true of the commit only, not of the checkout. The tree also carries tracked ANALYSIS/ (10 files) and EXPERIMENTS/ (5 files) material. No glob over **/authorization.json exists in the frozen code, so nothing in the execution chain reads the stale file.

The 20-file freeze-set aggregate e1b75b8b... cannot be recomputed from frozen artefacts alone: its rule (sha256 over sorted '<path>\0<sha256>\n') is defined only in CODE/work/WP-LEO-V2-PRE-EXPERIMENT-TRUST/round4/generate_freeze_scope.py, which FREEZE-SCOPE.md sec.4 explicitly excludes from the freeze. The criteria file states the rule for the execution-chain aggregate but not for this one; I had to read the unfrozen generator to reproduce it (it does reproduce exactly).

It is documented in compile_trace's docstring but not in materialization_report's own, and an independent verifier recomputing evidence the obvious way hits a spurious failure (I did).
